hints: If the bookings were listed in order of start time, which bookings could possibly need fusing with the one you are looking at?

Sort the slots by start. Then walk through them keeping one 'current block': each new slot either touches/overlaps the current block (extend its end) or starts after it (close the block and open a new one).

1. Sort slots by start time.
  2. Start the current block as the first slot.
  3. For each next slot: if its start ≤ current end, set current end = max(current end, slot end).
  4. Otherwise save the current block and make this slot the new current block.
  5. Save the last block and return all saved blocks.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Repeatedly scan every pair of blocks and fuse any two that overlap, until a full pass makes no change.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Sort by start, then a single left-to-right sweep that extends or closes the current block.

explain: Sample 1 sorted is [1,4],[3,6],[8,12],[12,13]. Start with [1,4]; [3,6] starts at 3 ≤ 4 so the block grows to [1,6]. [8,12] starts after 6, so [1,6] is saved and [8,12] becomes current; [12,13] starts at 12 ≤ 12 (touching counts) so it grows to [8,13]. After sorting, a slot can only overlap the block just before it, which is why one pass is enough. Watch the edge case where a later slot lies completely inside the current block: use max for the end, never just the new end.
recognize: Intervals in random order that must be combined when they overlap → sort by start and sweep, merging into the last block.
